claims.claim: Crawl access, indexability directives, and a 200 response are prerequisites to page optimization.
Direct LLM retrieval should be tested with the URL and one returned fact should be verified against the page.
The method checks Google, Bing, and Brave indexation plus HTML/server-rendered text and a self-canonical.
The page type should match dominant live-SERP intent and visible SERP features.
Freshness is investigated through visible dates and stale years in page source.
Transactional pages are evaluated for scannability, headline/CTA prominence, link affordances, trust, and goal completion.
Median competitor word count is used as a context range while the leaner viable end is preferred.
Grammar, heading hierarchy, mobile speed, and audience reading level are part of on-page readiness.
Keyword placement is baseline; relevant-topic coverage and brand context determine whether an AI draft is useful.
Click-to-call, form submission, thank-you flow, and confirmation email are tested as conversion continuity.
The demo compares a lean AI draft against a longer original and requires a one-to-two-hour human editorial pass.
The speaker's personal allocation assigns 5% to on-page, 20% to content quality, 20% to topical authority, 5% to technical SEO, 25% to backlinks, and 25% to third-party signals.
claims.boundary: Personal opinion; not an outcome model.
